name: Battle of Vienna (1683)
note: The plan shows the day of 12 September 1683 on the ground north and west of the city. The relief army is drawn on the west and north because the accounts put the Poles to the west of the Türkenschanze, the Saxons and Bavarians to the northwest and the Austrians to the north, with the Ottoman main camp further south. The accounts give no map positions for the villages, the forest or the hills, so each is placed on the side the story needs; the accounts do not say exactly where they lay. Which wing of the Ottoman army lay where is not stated beyond the Ottoman right flank, which the Polish infantry attacked. Numbers of troops differ widely between sources and are not shown. Paths are drawn straight; the accounts give no routes.

phases.title: The Ottoman army attacks before the allies are deployed
phases.text: The Ottoman army attacked early, seeking to disrupt the allied deployment. The imperial troops on the left and in the centre met the attack while the Polish troops were still coming into place.
phases.quote: At 4:00 am on 12 September, the Ottoman army attacked, seeking to interfere with the deployment of allied troops.

phases.title: The imperial army counterattacks in the north
phases.text: The Germans were the first to counterattack. After heavy fighting and several Ottoman counterattacks, the imperial army took the fortified villages of Nussdorf and Heiligenstadt.
phases.quote: The Germans were the first to counterattack.

phases.title: The Ottomans counterattack and assault the city
phases.text: By midday the imperial army had done significant damage and come close to a breakthrough. Mustafa Pasha counterattacked with most of his forces but held back elite Janissary and Sipahi units for an assault on the city.
phases.quote: Mustafa Pasha launched counterattacks with most of his forces, but held back some of the elite Janissary and Sipahi units for a simultaneous assault on the city

phases.title: Polish infantry advances on the Ottoman right
phases.text: Polish infantry advanced against the Ottoman right flank. Parts of the Ottoman army kept attacking the city, which let the Poles move forward, and by 4:00 pm they held Gersthof.
phases.quote: In the early afternoon, a large engagement started on the other side of the battlefield as the Polish infantry advanced on the Ottoman right flank.

phases.title: The imperial left presses on to the Türkenschanze
phases.text: The Germans resumed the offensive on the left at 3:30 pm. They met fierce resistance at first, then advanced by 5:00 pm and took Unterdöbling and Oberdöbling, closing on the central Ottoman position.
phases.quote: However, by 5:00 pm they had begun to advance and taken the villages of Unterdöbling and Oberdöbling.

phases.title: Hussars probe the Ottoman line
phases.text: The Polish cavalry came out of the forest, and a detachment of 120 hussars made a probing charge that showed the Ottomans could be attacked, at the cost of many casualties. The vizier left the Türkenschanze for the main camp.
phases.quote: At 4:00 pm, a detachment of 120 hussars engaged in a probing charge, successfully proving Ottoman vulnerability to attack but taking many casualties.

phases.title: The cavalry charges down the hills
phases.text: The king ordered the cavalry to attack in four contingents, three Polish and one from the Holy Roman Empire. The horsemen charged down the hills towards the Ottoman lines.
phases.quote: the Polish king ordered the cavalry to attack in four contingents, three Polish groups and one from the Holy Roman Empire

phases.title: The Ottoman lines break
phases.text: The charge quickly broke the battle lines of the Ottomans, who were already exhausted and demoralised, and they began to retreat from the battlefield. The hussars of the probing charge left the plan.
phases.quote: The charge quickly broke the battle lines of the Ottomans, who were already exhausted and demoralized and began to retreat from the battlefield.

phases.title: The cavalry rides for the camps
phases.text: The cavalry headed directly towards the Ottoman camps and the headquarters of Kara Mustafa, while the remaining Viennese garrison sallied out of its defences to join in the assault.
phases.quote: The cavalry headed directly towards the Ottoman camps and Kara Mustafa's headquarters, while the remaining Viennese garrison sallied out of its defenses to join in the assault.
